So here's what I, you know, said for the several months out on the campaign trail, if there were a magic wand on inflation, it would have been waived already. Just passing a bill that says make inflation go away isn't going to work isn't going to happen. In fact, Congress and the Biden administration tried that with the so-called inflation reduction act, which I argue actually made things worse. And even President Biden says was misnamed. It really wasn't about inflation. It was about green energy and other priorities that he had. Setting that aside, I think that the answer to what do we do is the old adage when you're in a hole, stop digging. And one of the things that drives inflation, it's not the only driver, but it is one of the drivers, is the huge increase in volume in federal spending over the last three and a half years roughly, coupled with the fact that most of that spending, or at least much of it, I shouldn't say most, I don't have that number in my head, but much of it, is deficit finance. We're not paying for it, and so it's paid for with either money that's borrowed from abroad or that's printed functionally. All of those are inflationary ingredients that go into the soup and drive it, and all of those are things that Congress can either control or influence. So, I do think that a focus on spending and on deficits is the smartest thing we can do in terms of, you know, trying to make a difference on the inflationary numbers going forward. And, you know, I've been really encouraged that so far, Mr. Musk, Mr. Ramaswami, the two who are leading this doge effort and all of that.
